# PlotSpectra – UAV plot analytics for Pix4Dfields outputs

*Generated by Ali Bazrafkan | ali.bazrafkan@montana.edu* — this credit is stamped on every figure (footer and PNG
metadata), on the README sheet of each workbook, in GeoTIFF tags and in the app header.

A local HTML app for plot-level phenotyping from Pix4Dfields exports. It computes zonal statistics of
15 literature-ranked vegetation indices, the raw bands, thermal temperature, a generated DTM and plant
height for every plot. It then tests whether plots differ significantly, renders 350 dpi figures, and
writes everything to one Excel workbook. Optional modules cover stand count, canopy cover and volume,
harvestable area, plant/canopy length, correlation matrices, thermal stress indices, GDD and field-data
integration.

The interface is a single HTML page (`app/index.html`). It talks to a small local Python engine
(`app/server.py`), because the heavy raster work, Esri File Geodatabase reading and GPU access need
GDAL/rasterio and Python. Your data stays on this computer: the only network calls are the free
Open-Meteo / NASA POWER weather APIs, made only when GDD or weather-based thermal analysis is on.

## Start (see QUICKSTART.md for the one-page version)

1. Install Python 3.10+ (python.org; on Windows tick "Add python.exe to PATH").
2. Double-click **`PlotSpectra.bat`** (Windows) or **`PlotSpectra.command`** (macOS/Linux). The first start creates a
   private environment in `.venv` and installs the packages; later starts take seconds. The app opens at
   http://127.0.0.1:8765. Options: `PlotSpectra.bat --port 8800 --no-browser`.
3. To share the app, run `python tools/make_share_zip.py` and send `dist/PlotSpectra_v*.zip` (~0.15 MB, no data).
4. To publish on GitHub, run `python tools/make_release.py`: it writes `dist/release_v*/` with the app zip, the
   1.3 GB sample data cut into 90 MB parts (GitHub refuses files over 100 MB), SHA-256 checksums, the join tools and
   `DOWNLOAD_AND_USE.md` for your users. Commit the source, attach that folder's files to a GitHub Release.

## Workflow (the numbered sections of the app)

1. **Data**: choose the Pix4D export folder and click *Scan*. The scan finds the multispectral
   `*.data.tif`, the DSM, the RGB orthomosaic, the band names (Green, Red, Red edge, NIR, Thermal IR,
   Alpha…), GSD, CRS, image date and centre. Band mapping can be overridden.
2. **Plots**: load the plot boundaries (`.shp`, `.geojson/.json`, `.gpkg`, `.kml` or a `.gdb` folder)
   and choose the **PLOTID** column. Optional columns:
   - treatment/genotype: enables the proper ANOVA/Tukey design
   - block/replicate: RCBD
   - sowing date: per-plot GDD
   - a negative edge buffer, to drop border rows
3. **Indices & stats**: the 15 indices from the literature panel are pre-selected (see below). You can
   also add custom formulas, choose all pixels or vegetation-only pixels, set the vegetation threshold,
   and configure the significance testing.
4. **Visualization**: choose figure families and the palette. Every figure is a **350 dpi PNG**.
   Raster export (GeoTIFF, full resolution) is **off unless you toggle it on and tick layers**.
5. **Advanced (optional)**: stand counting, canopy cover and volume, harvestable area, plant length,
   correlation matrix, thermal analysis, GDD, field-data integration. This section also holds the GPU,
   thread and DTM settings.
6. **Run**: live progress and log; you can cancel.
7. **Results**: Excel download and a gallery with tabs, search and a zoomable lightbox.

## GPU

On start the engine looks for **CuPy (CUDA) → PyTorch CUDA → PyTorch MPS (Apple) → NumPy CPU** and
uses the first one it finds. The header badge shows the device, and hovering it lists every GPU found.
Spectral index maths, per-plot statistics (sort-based median/percentiles) and the tiled GeoTIFF export
run on the GPU. File I/O and figure rendering are CPU-bound: they use worker threads and a process pool.
To enable an NVIDIA GPU: `pip install cupy-cuda12x`. The machine this was built on has no CUDA GPU, so
the GPU path is implemented but was **not run here**.

## What is computed

| Item | Method |
|---|---|
| Vegetation indices | NDVI, NDRE, GNDVI, SAVI, RVI, OSAVI, NGRDI, CIre, CIg, MSAVI2, DVI, MCARI, EVI2, TCARI/OSAVI, MTCI. These are ranked by use in Q1 UAV precision-agriculture papers, restricted to the G/R/RE/NIR bands available (no blue band). Formulas, DOIs and method: `docs/vegetation_indices_review.md` |
| Zonal statistics | min, mean, median, max, StDev, range per plot, **one Excel sheet per statistic** (rows = PLOTID). Pixel counts and plant-height p90/p95/p99 are added. |
| DTM | Bare-soil pixels (NDVI below the Otsu threshold, eroded) → low-percentile ground cells (1 m) → 2-pass outlier rejection → Delaunay interpolation + smoothing → bilinear sampling at full resolution. A QC figure is produced. |
| Plant height | DSM − generated DTM on vegetation pixels. The `06_plant_height` figure folder holds the DSM map, the DTM map, the canopy-height map, a histogram and a three-panel DSM → DTM → CHM figure on a shared elevation scale with hillshade. |
| Thermal | Unit auto-detected (Pix4Dfields gives centi-Kelvin) with a 6×MAD outlier filter. Canopy and soil temperature use stricter, eroded NDVI masks. |
| Significance | **Mode A** (PLOTID only): sub-plot cell means as replicates, Welch ANOVA / Kruskal–Wallis, Games–Howell or Dunn post-hoc, compact letters. This mode is descriptive because of pseudo-replication. **Mode B** (treatment column): plot means as replicates, CRD or RCBD ANOVA, assumption checks, Tukey / Games–Howell / Dunn, letters. Benjamini–Hochberg is applied across variables. Spec: `docs/viz_stats_spec.md` |

**Advanced modules**

| Module | Method |
|---|---|
| Stand count | Plant objects (connected components). Clumps are split by a field-wide single-plant area learned from open plots. Plots with closed canopy (>60 % cover) are reported as *not estimable* rather than given a wrong number. An NDVI-peak method is also available. |
| Canopy cover / volume | Vegetation fraction; Σ(height × pixel area) |
| Harvestable area | Canopy area (optionally taller than a cutting height) ÷ plot area |
| Plant / canopy length | Canopy extent along the plot's long axis, row coverage %, gaps longer than a threshold, mean and max plant-object length |
| Correlation | Pearson or Spearman, within each plot (pixels; Fisher-z mean) and across plots (plot means, with p-values). Redundant pairs (\|r\| ≥ 0.9) are flagged. |
| Thermal (advanced) | CTD; image-based CWSI (field coolest 5 % = Twet, Tair + 5 °C = Tdry); Idso CWSI (crop baselines); Ig, I3, NRCT, DACT; QC flags |
| GDD | Open-Meteo ERA5 archive, with the forecast API for recent days and NASA POWER as fallback (free, no key). Base / upper temperatures for 29 crops come from a literature review by the panel (`docs/gdd_tbase_review.md`, machine-readable `docs/gdd_tbase.json`); the app shows the source, DOI/URL and confidence for the chosen crop, and writes them to the GDD sheet. Six crops (hemp, camelina, safflower, millet, faba bean, rye) are low confidence. Per-plot sowing dates supported. Spec: `docs/thermal_gdd_spec.md` |
| Field data | CSV/Excel joined on a common column. Every numeric image metric is appended, with a match-status column and trait-correlation figures. |

## Outputs (in the output folder)

- `PlotStats_<timestamp>.xlsx`, with these sheets:
  - README
  - Minimum, Mean, Median, Maximum, StDev, Range, PixelCount
  - PlantHeight_Pctl, Canopy_Structure
  - Thermal_Advanced, GDD, Weather_Daily
  - Stats_Design, Stats_Omnibus, Stats_Letters, Stats_PlotSummary, Stats_GroupSummary, Stats_Pairs, PW_<var>
  - Corr_*
  - Integrated_FieldData
  - Indices_Reference, Failed_Plots
- `PlotPredictors_<timestamp>.xlsx`: **one row per PLOTID with every numeric predictor** (all six statistics of every
  band/index/height/thermal variable, height percentiles, canopy structure, thermal indices, GDD, plus the field-data
  traits prefixed `Field_` when supplied). Sheets: Predictors, Dictionary (column definitions), About. The same table is
  also the `All_Predictors` sheet of the main workbook.
- `figures/` (350 dpi PNG), organised in sub-folders:
  `01_overview`, `02_index_maps`, `03_plot_maps`, `04_distributions_tests`, `05_rankings`, `06_plant_height`,
  `07_thermal`, `08_canopy_structure`, `09_correlation` (+ `per_plot`), `10_gdd`, `11_field_data`;
  gallery thumbnails in `figures/_thumbs/`, index in `figures/manifest.json`
- `rasters/*.tif`, only if requested
- `last_config.json`. The *Save settings* / *Load* buttons reuse a configuration.

## Notes and limits

- **Thermal data on the test flight**: canopy reads about 12 °C below air temperature, so the Idso
  CWSI is negative. The app raises the `thermal_offset_suspect` and `thermal_cold_tail` flags. Rely on
  the relative indices (image-based CWSI, NRCT, plot rankings), or supply a calibrated offset with the
  *Custom* unit.
- **Image date**: taken from the TIFF tag. Check it in the GDD section, because Pix4D may write the
  processing time.
- **Stand counting**: only meaningful before canopy closure.
- **Plant length**: measured along the plot's long axis, which assumes rows run along it.
- **Synthetic test data**: `tests/make_test_plots.py` builds plots and a synthetic field-data file from
  the sample orthomosaic. `tests/run_headless.py` runs the whole pipeline without the UI.
